Ugh — that sounds exhausting. You did the right thing by stepping away. Small rituals and quick body-focused tools can help shut down a wired shift.

Try a short routine you can do right after work:
- 60-second sensory ground: name 5 things you see, 4 you feel, 3 you hear, 2 you smell, 1 you taste.
- Box or paced breathing: inhale 4s, hold 4s, exhale 6–8s. Repeat 4–6 times.
- Quick tense-and-release: clench feet/legs for 5s, then relax. Work up the body.
- Change clothes and wash your face or take a warm shower — physical transition helps the brain switch off.
- Do a 2-minute “brain dump”: jot whatever’s racing in one sentence each. Close the notebook.

If you can’t sleep after lying there 20–30 minutes, get up and do a low-stim activity (read, light stretching) until you feel tired. If this wired feeling keeps happening often, consider talking to someone about it. Feel better soon.

- “I use they/them pronouns.”  
- “Just a heads-up: I go by they/them.”  
- “Please use they/them — thanks.”  
- If they repeat it: “That’s not my pronoun; I’m they/them.”  
- If manager’s watching and you want minimal fuss: “Quick correction: I use they/them.”  

Keep your tone flat and steady. Practice them a couple times in the mirror so they land automatically.

For sleep when you’re wired from caffeine: do 4 rounds of 4‑7‑8 breathing (inhale 4s, hold 7s, exhale 8s). Then try the cognitive shuffle: imagine random, neutral objects (apple, brick, lamp, shoe…) one at a time, for 1–2 seconds each. Finish with a slow feet-to-head body scan, relaxing each part on the exhale. Dim lights and avoid screens; if you’re awake 20–30 minutes, get up and do a low-stim activity until sleepy. You’ve got this.

1) Change into comfy clothes, splash/wash your face (30–45s).  
2) 60-second 5-4-3-2-1 grounding (name 5 things you see, 4 you feel…)
